FINDING: rev 1.4's chalk house glyph on the p03 cache board solved the beat (P7 under 60s, zero random clicking) by REPLACING the bearing hop rather than teaching it -- P8 verbatim, 'because it had a house mark on it', with no reference to the III bearing, and P11 at z1, 'did I read it as a direction? no -- never'. Consequence at p04 (P12): the ABSENCE of a chalk mark read as an UNMET PRECONDITION ('the mark hasn't been triggered -- there must be another step'), sending the player out of the zone for 8-15 minutes on a sole-thread chokepoint that also gates the oil can, the gear frame and p06's own tally-readout safety net. FIX: couple the dormer mark to the HAND. The board's chalk note becomes a chalk hub dot + the canonical hand-hour silhouette in chalk value, laid at the SAME rendered attitude as the hand composited on the ring, with its tip ABUTTING the canonical chalk die-house -- one composite, the SAME clu-watch-a gate, the SAME single appearance event, no new state and no earlier tell. It is a scale model of the projection drawn ON the board, NOT a sight-line: the ring is at eye height and the board on the floor, so no honest chalk line connects them in world OR image space, and the rev-B 'considered and rejected: chalk sight-line' finding STANDS UNREVERSED. The device reuses the level's own established habit of running one glyph through three materials (the house glyph is already engraved on the watch, carved on the beam and chalked on the board; the hand is now both laid across the ring and chalked on the board). EXPECTED EFFECT: difficulty at p03 ~0 (it stays 3.5 -- the board is already marked and is already a single always-correct hotspot; nothing changes what to click or when), and NEGATIVE stall at p04, which is the entire point: with the grammar taught, C3's already-shipping wide-view hand echo at the gear ring is the instrument the player reaches for, and no-mark reads as learned grammar rather than as a locked state. The level score is UNCHANGED at 6.0 PROVISIONAL and this delta does NOT release the progression-ledger.md write. Probe P12 is rewritten to verify the teach; it is the measurement that settles this delta.

theme: A tower clockmaker's attic workshop above the town. Every clock in the room stopped at the same moment. The attic backs directly onto the tower's great dial; the whole room is one connected machine of linkage rods, gears and chimes that the clockmaker left mid-thought. A gray cat still lives here.
framing_line: All his clocks stopped at six.
time_of_day: Late golden afternoon. Low warm sun through the dormer window (required: the cat's sunbeam patch, p02 staging); the great dial in z3 glows amber with transmitted daylight (required: mirrored-numeral legibility, p09).

win_condition.description: The attic's only exit, the stair door, is barred by a vault-style TIME LOCK connected by visible linkage rods to the tower movement behind the wall. Restore the great clock -- oil and wind it, set its hands to the release time shown on the clockmaker's 'will return' tag (set from BEHIND the mirrored dial), and start the pendulum. The strike train fires, the linkage lifts the door bar, and the player leaves down the stairs with the cat.

clue_gating.policy_revision: inherits L1 rev-1.3 policy (viewed_definition, persistence, D6/D7 semantics); no_tell_rule amended at rev 1.3 (playtest tweak 1, user-approved)
clue_gating.purpose: Protect code-like entries and sweep-brute-force surfaces from lucky/spoiler shortcuts while never false-blocking an earned solve. Gates reference only clues that carry the code's actual information.
clue_gating.viewed_definition: A clue counts as VIEWED the moment its designated close-up view has been displayed at least once. No dwell time, no comprehension check, no timers. Multi-instance clues count when ANY instance is displayed.
clue_gating.no_tell_rule: Gated attempts replay the puzzle's EXISTING failure grammar with no distinguishing tell -- IN FULL for p07 and p09, and for every WRONG spot at p03/p04. REV 1.3 AMENDMENT (playtest tweak 1): the CORRECT board (p03) and CORRECT brick (p04) are the single sanctioned exception -- a pre-clue pry there produces a FAINT-TELL (slight creak + perceptible shift, still firmly not yielding; see D10). Rationale: the playtest's impatient-pryer variant showed a pure no-tell on the correct spot lets an early pry CERTIFY the spot as inert, poisoning the later watch clue (15-25 min stall, 'the game lied to me'). The faint-tell leaves a memory hook without reading as an invitation. The code-entry gates (p07, p09) remain strictly no-tell.
clue_gating.ungated_rationale_class: Free pickups, tool-on-hotspot oiling, tile seating with pop-back, the cat beat, mechanism completions (winding, pendulum push), and the gear train (a mechanically TRUE configuration must work when built -- gating physical truth reads as a broken machine) are physical acts, not code entries.
clue_gating.art_impact: Rev 1.3: two micro-cues added, both SFX/haptic-tier plus one line of animation each -- the correct-spot faint-tell at p03/p04 (D10) and the cat's mouse-offer tell (D3). Everything else reuses existing failure states (wrong boards/bricks stay dead; vault wheels spin without the hatch releasing; hand-setting does not trigger the strike -- though see D11 for the wound+swinging ambient layer, which is state feedback, not gate feedback). REV 1.4 (scoped clause -- NOT a general permission class): three named annotations are CLUE-STATE RENDERS, not gate tells -- (i) the canonical hour hand on the z1 house ring in the wide view, (ii) the clockmaker's chalk note on the p03 cache board in the wide and the close-up -- at rev 1.4.1 a chalk hub dot plus a chalk bearing hand plus the chalk house glyph, ONE composite -- both functions of clu-watch-a, and (iii) the canonical hour hand on the z2 gear ring in the wide view, a function of clu-watch-b. They render on view entry, never in response to an attempt, so no_tell_rule is untouched: the wrong-spot dead wall and the D10 correct-spot faint-tell are byte-stable, and the pre-clue experience is byte-identical to rev 1.3. p07 AND p09 REMAIN STRICTLY NO-ANNOTATION -- their gates protect code entries where any post-view annotation is spoiler-equivalent. Any future clue-state render requires Validator re-verification. REV 1.4.1 (teach-at-dormer, user-approved 2026-08-08): NO new clue-state render is added. The CONTENT of named render (ii) changes -- on the SAME clu-watch-a gate, in the SAME single appearance event, on the SAME overlay ids, with no new state -- so this clause's scope is unchanged and NO new permission class is created. The re-verification this clause requires has been performed: Validator delta-check of Designer spec rev B.1, CONFIRMED, 0 Critical, 2026-08-08. p07 AND p09 REMAIN STRICTLY NO-ANNOTATION.

BINDING LAYOUT RULES: the hand's rendered attitude must match the RENDERED attitude of the C1 ring hand in the same plate to within +/- 5 degrees (match the two RENDERED marks, NOT world horizontal -- the ring is drawn in perspective, and the rhyme between the two marks is the entire mechanism); the hand's tip must ABUT the house glyph's left edge (touching or slightly overlapping, within one glyph-width) and must NEVER overshoot it or run toward the rect edge, because a pointer that runs off reads 'keep going further right' at a floorboard field; the WHOLE note sits wholly inside the ov-cache-* rect, so what is marked is exactly what is tappable (no new hotspot, no M1 re-registration); keep a visible waist between the hand's tip and the house's outline so that at wide scale the note reads as TWO PARTS rather than one blob. IF IT WILL NOT FIT: shorten the HAND, floor at the house glyph's own width; then close hub-to-house spacing to zero; NEVER shrink the house glyph below its RF-7(a) wide-legible size; if it still will not fit, escalate to the Designer -- do not improvise. The CLOSE-UP (cu-floor-cache) renders the SAME note larger and must NOT elaborate it (no added notches, strokes, ticks or second hand); present-in-both or absent-from-both in every state. COLOUR-BLIND: hand and house are told apart by SHAPE and POSITION only; identical chalk value, stroke weight and luminance floor; the hand is NEVER faded, ghosted, dashed, translucent or lower-opacity than the house; no glow, flash or colour change, on appearance or ever. nodes.name: The automaton gear train
nodes.mechanic: gear-ratio reasoning (two-stage reduction; meshing train) -- LEVEL SIGNATURE MECHANIC (user ratified as the arithmetic peak, flag #2)
nodes.input: Mount one gear on POST A (meshing the crank's fixed 12-tooth pinion; POST A carries a fixed coaxial 8-tooth pinion) and one on POST B (meshed by that pinion, driving the cam). Then crank through one full cam revolution.

nodes.derivation: Slate: (A/12) x (B/8) = 24 -> A x B = 2304. Available: rack {16, 24, 36, 40, 48, 72} + the found 64-tooth great wheel. Unique pair anywhere in the level: 36 x 64 (the 36 is on the rack; the 64 must be found via p03 -- the great wheel is strictly required; the playtest confirmed 'no rack pair works, so a 64 must be hidden somewhere' lands as the intended deduction). The 48 tempts 48 x 48 = 2304 exactly, but only one 48 exists (rh-48-gear).
clues: stamped tooth counts (Arabic) + physically countable teeth on every loose gear
Roman XII / VIII stamps on the fixed pinions

live mechanical feedback: with ANY meshing pair mounted the crank turns and the cam/mural visibly runs at the resulting speed; REV 1.4 -- 'countable' is now realized ON SCREEN by the D13 live crank-tally readout (one chalk stroke per crank revolution in the current cam cycle), because the build ran a whole cam cycle on one press with no countable artifact (playtest 2b: the counting path is a legitimate no-algebra solve route, and D13 is what delivers it)
clu-frame-tally (F3: the chalked 24:1 target proportion restated on the frame's own cheek)

clue_gate.rationale: Mechanical truth: a correctly built 24:1 train MUST work whether or not the slate was seen -- gating it would read as a broken machine. The brute-force surface (~30 ordered pairs, each needing a cranking test) is real but tedious, and the visible too-fast/too-slow cam feedback is INTENDED reasoning material, not a leak. User CONFIRMED ungated at checkpoint (flag #3). REV 1.4: the D13 tally readout is mechanical truth (the realized ratio of the mounted pair, identical in form for correct and incorrect pairs, with no proximity signal), so it too is UNGATED; gating it would reintroduce the broken-machine read this ungated rationale exists to prevent. clu-frame-tally is likewise non-gating and appears in no clue_gate.

yields.via: at exactly 24:1 the mural completes one full clean cycle (sun crosses the carved town, the watchman figure strikes his bell), a counterweight drops, and the wall panel swings open -- latches open permanently

nodes.failure_behavior: Wrong ratio: the cam visibly runs too fast or too slow; at cycle-end the panel latch ratchets and SLIPS with a clack (identical clack for every wrong ratio -- speed itself is the only differential feedback, by design). Gears freely remountable; rack gears return to the rack, the great wheel returns to inventory if unmounted. No lockout.

nodes.input: Turn the setting crank to position the great dial's hands (5-minute detents on the minute hand).

The player stands BEHIND the dial: numerals are visibly mirror-reversed (clu-mirrored-numerals), so naively copying the tag's hand positions onto the back view sets the front to 4:40 and nothing happens. The aha: mirror the tag (the playtest's unstick path: no legible 'VII' exists anywhere on the back view). Any-order verification: the strike fires the moment all three release conditions hold.

(Strict no-tell here is unchanged by the rev-1.3 pry-gate amendment; the D11 ambient is state feedback about the MOVEMENT, not about the entered time's correctness.)
clue_gate.rationale: 144 detent combinations plus the tag being on the required path (z4 precedes any possible knowledge of 7:20) means the gate can never false-block; it closes the persistent-fiddling/spoiler path only.

developer_notes.topic: Cat refusal grammar + mouse-offer tell (rev 1.3, playtest tweak 2, user-approved)
developer_notes.note: Baseline (unchanged for everything except the mouse): nudging the cat OR offering ANY non-mouse inventory item produces the identical terminal refusal (one slow blink, resettles heavier); offered items return unspent; no escalation or variation across repeats. REV 1.3 EXCEPTION -- itm-toy-mouse offered DIRECTLY to the cat: the cat's eyes LOCK onto the mouse and visibly track it, tail flicks once or twice, body stays put; the mouse returns to inventory. Identical tell on every repeat (no escalation into pouncing -- the offer never executes p02). The tell is one line of animation distinct from the slow blink; its message is 'interested in THIS, but not like that', steering toward wind-and-place-on-floor. Petting: purr, no state change, always available. After p02 the cat sits by the stair door; baseline refusal grammar applies there (the mouse is gone by then, so the exception is moot).

Three mouse interactions, all loss-free until the solve: (1) offered DIRECTLY to the cat (armed-item use on the cat hotspot): D3 tell fires, mouse returns to inventory, p02 does NOT execute; (2) wound and placed on the floor anywhere NOT near the cat: skitters a small circle and returns to inventory automatically; (3) wound and placed on the FLOOR near the cat's bench: p02 fires, mouse leaves inventory permanently (cat keeps it -- it has no other uses; declared soft-lock-safe).

With any meshing pair mounted and the arbor freed, cranking runs the mural at the true resulting ratio -- visible speed IS intended feedback (mechanical truth, not a leak). Every wrong ratio ends its cam cycle with the SAME latch-slip clack; only speed differs. The cranks-per-clack cadence must be consistent and countable (playtest 2b: counting toward the slate's 24 tallies is a sanctioned no-algebra solve route). Gears mount/unmount freely; rack gears live in the apparatus (never inventory); the great wheel returns to inventory when unmounted. The fixed pinions (XII, VIII) are not removable. REV 1.4: 'countable' is now realized ON SCREEN, not only in audio -- see D13. The build-16 implementation ran a whole cam cycle on ONE press with no countable artifact, so the sanctioned no-algebra route (playtest 2b) was specified and never delivered; D13 delivers it. Note the rack-only straddle that makes the counting route close honestly: no rack-only pair reads 24, and the two nearest bracket it (40x48 = 20 below, 36x72 = 27 above), so a counting player hits a hard numerical bracket and must conclude that a wheel they do not have exists elsewhere.

Inherit L1 D6 verbatim: gated puzzles re-evaluate (gate AND solution) on every input/attempt event AND on entry into the puzzle's close-up. Stale cases here: p07 (wheels pre-set correctly while gated) and p09 (front 7:20 pre-set while gated). p03/p04 have none (pry is an explicit act).

Inherit L1 D7: one persistent saved boolean per gating clue (clu-watch-a, clu-watch-b, clu-master-time, clu-worldclock-row, clu-return-tag). Set on first display of the qualifying view; never cleared; ordinary satisfiable requirements. (Rev 1.2: the non-gating clu-face-convention flag is deleted with its node.)

The z1 stair door must never accept item use or code input: its housing has no keyhole (art requirement). Any interaction while barred: the bar rattles once against the linkage -- identical every time, pointing attention up the rods (the door teaches 'solve me elsewhere').

developer_notes.topic: Live crank-tally readout (rev 1.4, F4 -- user-approved A1; delivers the counting route D5 and playtest 2b have promised since rev 1.0)
developer_notes.note: PRESENTATION ONLY. A chalk tally block on the gear-frame cheek, directly beneath the F3 crib and separated from it by a visible baseline. ACCRUAL: measured as ACCUMULATED CRANK ROTATION SINCE THE LAST CAM CLACK -- one full chalk stroke per full turn of accumulated rotation, remainder drawn as ONE partial stroke. Counting crossings of a fixed index mark on the crank is PROHIBITED: it drifts in phase and produces a 7/7/6 oscillation across cycles. Because every cam cycle of a given pair consumes exactly R = A*B/96 crank revolutions, the accumulated-rotation measure renders the IDENTICAL picture every cycle -- nothing oscillates. NON-INTEGER PAIRS (exactly three of the 21): 16x40 = 6 2/3 -> 6 full + one partial; 16x64 = 10 2/3 -> 10 full + one partial; 40x64 = 26 2/3 -> 26 full + one partial. All other 18 pairs are integers; the SOLUTION 36x64 = exactly 24 full strokes with NO partial. The partial stroke is a FIXED CANONICAL GLYPH: same chalk value, width and slot pitch, drawn UPRIGHT (never diagonal -- it is not a strike and cannot collide with the five-group closing strike) at a CONSTANT height; its height MUST NOT be derived from the residue at runtime (V17-W1: a proportional height would silently turn height into a variable signal channel if the gear set ever changed). It shares the full strokes' baseline and is shortened at the top only (V17-W3). It must NOT be faded, ghosted, dashed or lower-opacity -- that would swap the form cue for a value cue -- and must hold >=3:1 luminance in its own right in BOTH wide and close-up views. It never receives a five-group diagonal and is never counted into a group of five. Non-integrality is mechanical truth, NOT a proximity signal -- 6 2/3 (far) and 26 2/3 (near) render identically in form. PERSISTENCE: the block is TRANSIENT VIEW/SESSION STATE of the same class as an animation frame -- NEVER written to the save, NEVER readable by any gate, condition, requirement or D7 flag; on save/load it re-derives to EMPTY. What is drawn is a pure function of (currently mounted pair, accumulated rotation since the last clack). The completed-cycle count STAYS DRAWN -- so a player who looked away still gets the number -- until any of: (i) any mount or unmount at either post (clears immediately and completely; the frame must NEVER display a count belonging to a configuration that is no longer mounted), (ii) fewer than two gears mounted (no pair, nothing drawn), (iii) scene reload or save load, (iv) the start of the next crank press (redraws from zero). LEAK CONSTRAINTS: identical in form for correct and incorrect pairs; never varies with closeness to 24; never varies with any clue-viewed flag; UNGATED, exactly as p06 is ungated. NO GLOW, FLASH OR COLOUR CHANGE when the count reaches 24 (RF-7c) -- success differentiation stays with the latch taking and the panel opening. LEGIBILITY / TEDIUM: worst case across the whole gear set is 48 STROKES (64x72 = 4608/96 = 48; it is NOT 54 -- that would require two 72-tooth gears and only one exists). The block must stay legible at 48 via the five-grouping; the accrual animation must be skippable/fast-forwardable and the final block fully readable STATICALLY without having watched it accrue (RC-4). One crank press = one full cam cycle -- do NOT implement per-turn tapping. Renders in cu-gear-frame and in the wide if the crank is operable there; the crib and the live block are distinguished by POSITION ONLY (visible baseline/gap), NEVER by hue or chalk value, and must never read as one continuous block of 24+N strokes (RF-7b).

colorblind_safety: No puzzle uses color differentiation anywhere. Gears differ by SIZE + countable teeth + stamped numerals; tiles by engraved numerals; world clocks by landmark SILHOUETTES + stamped offsets; vault wheels by pictogram headers + engraved numerals.
Brass vs bronze vs steel finishes are ambient only, never load-bearing.
Mirrored-dial reading depends on numeral SHAPE reversal, not color.
Cat/mouse, oiling, winding: state changes are shape/motion (weight height, pendulum motion, bar position), never color.
All four landmark pictograms (Big Ben, Burj Khalifa, Statue of Liberty, Mt Fuji) are silhouette-distinct at close-up size -- shape only, no color reliance.
Rev 1.3 cues are audio/haptic/motion (creak+shift, eye-track+tail-flick, tick+twitch) -- no color channel involved.

Rev 1.4 chalk marks (slate regrouping, frame crib, live tally block, cache-board chalk note -- bearing hand plus house glyph, rev 1.4.1) are luminance-contrast strokes and canonical glyph SHAPES, counted by quantity and grouped by shape; no color channel is load-bearing and no mark is distinguished from another by hue. The rev-1.4 p03/p04 pointer annotations are glyph shape and pointer ANGLE against a 12-notch ring.

RF-7(a) LUMINANCE FLOOR (mandatory): every rev-1.4 chalk element must hold >= 3:1 luminance contrast against its LOCAL substrate in BOTH the wide and the close-up. The slate is safe by construction; the two risk surfaces are the gear-frame TIMBER CHEEK and the WORN FLOORBOARD IN RAKING LIGHT, and the fallback NB 'blend chalk onto worn timber' edit is exactly the operation that could erode it. Discrimination must NEVER rest on the warm/cool hue difference between chalk and timber.

RF-7(b) BLOCK SEPARATION (mandatory): the F3 crib block and the D13 live block are distinguished by POSITION -- a visible baseline, chalked rule or clear gap -- and NEVER by hue, chalk value, or an 'old chalk vs fresh chalk' treatment. They must never read as one continuous block of 24+N strokes. Distinguishing them by value or hue would be a color-only distinction on a load-bearing comparison.

RF-7(c) NO SUCCESS COLOR CUE (mandatory): the live tally block must NOT glow, flash or change color when the count reaches 24. Success differentiation stays with the latch taking and the wall panel opening -- a color-carried success cue would be both a gate-adjacent tell and a color-only signal.
